Technical_Enrichment: Mahlkönig EK43 S (barista-confirmed) carries the same 98 mm flat cast-steel burr set as the full-size EK43 in a compact body — the largest burr diameter logged in the archive alongside the EK Omnia. A 98 mm burr presents roughly 2.3× the cutting surface area of a 64 mm burr, producing a narrow particle size distribution with very low fines yield; fines are the primary driver of micro-channelling and selective over-extraction of bitter chlorogenic acid lactones, so their suppression here is what preserved the cranberry signal as a clean single line rather than a muddied red-fruit blur. OREA flat-bottom (plastic body, barista-confirmed) contributes wide unrestricted drainage and even bed saturation across a shallow uniform bed. On the ratio: 1:13.8 sits well below the 1:15–1:17 Palate DNA band and is a concentrated format, yet the cup carried no bitter tail. The reason is process chemistry — Washed processing strips the cherry skin entirely before drying, so there is minimal procyanidin and tannin load available to enter solution. A concentrated ratio therefore amplifies malic and citric acid density (perceived as cranberry brightness) without an accompanying polyphenol penalty. The thermal stability across all three phases points to high organic acid concentration from slow high-altitude maturation in Rwanda's volcanic highlands, where cool nights extend the cherry ripening cycle and drive acid accumulation.

Technical_Enrichment: ARCHIVE-DEFINING METHOD ENTRY — FIRST FULL-IMMERSION SWITCH PROTOCOL LOGGED. House method confirmed directly by co-owner and barista Pei: 95°C water, EK43S setting #7 (fine), valve CLOSED, the entire 210–215 ml charge delivered in a SINGLE POUR OF 20 SECONDS with no pulsing, circling or agitation, undisturbed full immersion until 2:50, then valve opened for a single drawdown. Pour time was originally field-recorded as "30 seconds or less" and subsequently corrected to 20 s by Pei on 23 Aug 2026 — barista confirmation overrides field recall. CANDIDATE EXTRACTION LAW 10 — IMMERSION DECOUPLES GRIND SIZE FROM FLOW RATE: in percolation, grind governs surface area and drawdown rate simultaneously, so extraction yield cannot be pursued without paying in flow; with the valve shut there is no flow to choke, and fineness can be pushed to a level that would trigger apex choke in a conical cone. EK43S #7 would be reckless in a V60 and is unremarkable here. Two supporting mechanisms: (i) a static column cannot compact, so channelling and fines migration are structurally unavailable rather than merely avoided; (ii) colloids and lipids remain in suspension for the full steep instead of being progressively stripped and filtered by continuous flow — the origin of the body Pei explicitly optimises for. SYSTEM DESIGN NOTE: removing pour rate, pour pattern, agitation and pulse timing leaves only grind, temperature, water mass and a clock — variables that can be handed to a barista on a first shift. Applied team-wide with per-lot tuning only; a protocol engineered for cross-barista consistency rather than individual virtuosity. FERMENTATION FINDING — consistent with Entry #085 and contrary to Entry #082: anaerobic ferment failed to mask varietal expression, with orange and lime leading and no berry or wine register at any temperature. VARIETAL CAVEAT: this is a 70/30 Gesha-Typica blend, so varietal attribution is partial and the Typica fraction may account for some of the body and the mid-phase apple. Gesha_Alert fires on Gesha-dominant composition; the blend is flagged explicitly here to prevent downstream analysis reading it as a single-varietal Gesha lot. ORANGE/CITRUS CROSS-TERROIR NOTE: orange appears again here, now outside Ethiopia — open question whether this is a Gesha genetic marker rather than an Ethiopian terroir constant.

Cone preheated and filter rinsed (barista-confirmed), ratio 1:15 inside the Palate DNA band, EK43 98mm flat burr = benchmark hardware. The ascending two-stage profile OPENS AT 71°C, far below the threshold at which volatile monoterpenes mobilise. Limonene, linalool and gamma-terpinene carry yuzu's identity and require thermal energy both to extract from the bed and to achieve retronasal release; estragole/anethole carry tarragon and behave identically. The first pour — with full access to a fresh bed and the steepest concentration gradient — stripped the fast, low-volatility citric/malic acid fraction while leaving the aromatic fraction behind. What reached the cup was yuzu's ACID SKELETON with its aromatic signature removed, which reads as soft apple. Ratio: Slightly less than 1:17 (barista-confirmed — deviation from house standard on the day)
Official_Notes: Kaffir Lime | Yellow Peach | Jasmine | Earl Grey
Your_Verdict: HOT: Bright and acidic on the tongue. Lime hits immediately. Slight bitter tinge in the aftertaste. Possible trace of peach. Light body, disappears quickly. Technical_Enrichment: Bitterness attributed primarily to the green, with ratio as a contributing variable. Barista confirmed the brew ran slightly leaner than the 1:17 house standard on the day (approx 12.5g dose, 210–220g yield — exact figures uncertain), so this is NOT a clean single-variable comparison against the 05 Aug El Romerillo, which used house-standard 1:17 on identical hardware and finished with zero bitter tail. Two factors still point away from extraction as the primary cause: the bitterness was present from the HOT phase rather than emerging on cooling (concentration-driven bitterness typically builds as sweetness contrast fades), and it persisted in the mouth five minutes after the cup — a duration inconsistent with a marginal ratio shift and consistent with compounds structurally bound to the bean. The 'unripe lime' descriptor is diagnostic: bitterness fused to the citrus as pith/rind character, distinct from the flat, dry CGA lactone signature logged on the 08 Jul Natural Bourbon. Most consistent with underripe cherry in the lot — elevated chlorogenic acids and low sugar development, which washed processing conceals nothing of. Extraction physics otherwise near-ideal: Geisha's low bean density gives up volatiles readily at 93°C, and the OREA's wide unrestricted drain keeps contact time short, protecting monoterpenes. GESHA HYPOTHESIS: lime present in HOT and dominant by MID from Peruvian terroir, washed, no Ethiopian lineage — supports citrus as a genetic varietal marker rather than an Ethiopian terroir signature. Yellow peach appeared only as a trace in HOT, consistent with white peach being Guji-specific rather than a universal varietal fingerprint.

Grinder: Option-O LAGOM 01 (102mm Mizen Blind Burrs — largest flat burr in archive)
Official_Notes: Funk → Tropical Fruit → Pineapple (no printed note card; Bayu pop-up lot)
Your_Verdict: AROMA: Opened funky and fermented on the nose, then slowly resolved — tropical fruits emerged as the cup settled. The funk announced itself first and then stepped aside. HOT: Bright with a little funk still present, but tropical fruit already pushing through. MID: Tropical fruit takes over completely; the ferment character recedes. MID-COOL (BEST WINDOW): Pineapple emerges clearly and dominates — really fruity, generous, resolved. This was the peak of the cup and the most enjoyable phase. VERDICT: I liked this, and he did it very well. Amazing experience overall — great discussions with both Ong Shen Choy and Bayu Prawiro. Very satisfied and worth the visit.
Technical_Enrichment: ARCHIVE FIRST — SECOND NON-ARABICA SPECIES. Coffea Excelsa (Coffea liberica var. dewevrei lineage) is a distinct species, under 1% of world production and rarely roasted for specialty. Only the second non-Arabica in the archive after the Corner Corner Liberica (Entry #039). ASCENDING TEMPERATURE PROTOCOL — barista-confirmed by Bayu Prawiro: 4 pours, starting LOW at 75°C and climbing to 94°C. This is the exact INVERSE of Fluid's house architecture (70→90→70°C oscillating, or 93°C→65°C descending on the Finca Sophia). The chemistry maps precisely onto the cup experienced: the 75°C opening under-extracts the aggressive fermentation volatiles produced by thermal shock — which is why the funk was present on the nose and first sip but faded rather than built; the 94°C finish then pulls the heavier sugars out of a denser, non-Arabica bean structure, which is why tropical fruit and finally pineapple dominated the mid-cool phase. Funk down, fruit up, by design. LAW 6 AMENDED. Thermal Shock processing previously exceeded this palate's fermentation ceiling at Entry #059 (Finca El Diviso, Aji Bourbon, Oaks) under a DESCENDING protocol. Under an ASCENDING protocol it did not. The controlling variable is brew architecture, not the process itself. GRINDER — ARCHIVE FIRST: Option-O LAGOM 01 with 102mm Mizen blind burrs. Verified per Rule 6 (search-before-logging): official qualified filter grinder of the World Brewers Cup 2026–2029; blind burr format removes screw holes for ~18% more effective grinding surface vs the 98mm standard; independent testing records 0.5g retention and 0.04g standard deviation. Now the LARGEST FLAT BURR in the archive, ahead of the EK43/EK Omnia at 98mm and the Lagom P100 at 100mm. COMPETITION PROVENANCE: this exact coffee — Sumedang Excelsa — formed the final 10% of Bayu Prawiro's blend when he took 1st Runner-Up at the 2025 World Brewers Cup in Jakarta (70% Finca Sophia washed Geisha, 20% Janson Estate Panama anaerobic, 10% Sumedang Excelsa). Both other components appeared on today's pop-up menu, and the Finca Sophia backbone is already a joint #1 cup in this archive (1 Aug 2026, Fluid).
